customManagers.description: Talos version in versions.env -- the ONLY place this is tracked now. A Kustomize `replacements` block (config/kustomization.yaml) projects this into every SUC Plan's spec.version and talosctl image tag at build time, so there is no longer a separate manager for those; bumping this file is the whole update. The Factory installer tag in the machine configs (below) is the one pin Kustomize cannot reach and still needs its own manager. A bump here does NOT require regenerating SCHEMATIC_ID: the schematic ID is a content hash of the extension list and is independent of the Talos version -- the same ID serves v1.12.0 through v1.13.9. Only editing schematic.yaml changes it. The talos group is still never auto-merged, for the real reasons: the upgrade reboots nodes, and the Image Factory builds per (schematic, version) pair, so a brand-new release may have no image for these extensions yet. The Talos image workflow checks both.

Kubernetes control-plane/kubelet version in versions.env, upgraded independently of TALOS_VERSION via talosctl upgrade-k8s (plans/talos-kubernetes-upgrade.yaml). Grouped separately from talos and never auto-merged: the upgrade touches every node's control-plane components. This manager always proposes the newest kubernetes/kubernetes release it finds, with no notion of stepping one minor at a time -- Renovate has no setting for that on a raw regex-matched pin. talosctl upgrade-k8s only supports an N -> N or N -> N+1 minor step, so a PR from this manager that skips a minor is expected to fail the Talos image workflow's dedicated check, not something that check is a defensive fallback against.

Factory installer tag in the machine configs. Decides which Talos a rebuilt node installs, so leaving it behind versions.env means a rebuild lands on the old version and needs an immediate upgrade. This is the one pin Kustomize's replacements cannot reach: Talos machine config is applied by hand via talosctl, entirely outside Kustomize/Flux. The SCHEMATIC_ID in the same string is NOT tracked and must still be regenerated by hand whenever the schematic changes.

CloudNativePG cluster images. The built-in kubernetes manager only reads the `image:` key; CNPG Cluster resources spell it `imageName:`, so the two postgres pins (keycloak-pg, filer-meta-pg) were invisible to Renovate and drifted five patch releases behind -- 16.10 while 16.15 was current -- carrying 12 fixable critical CVEs between them. Every other image in the repo was kept current automatically; these two were the ones nothing was watching.

cilium-cli image used by the Talos cilium-install inlineManifest, which installs the CNI at first boot before Flux exists. This was cilium-cli-ci:latest -- an unpinned rolling CI build -- until it went distroless and broke bootstrap outright: the Job's shell form could no longer start. Pinning it is what stops the bootstrap path drifting under us again. Same file as the installer tag above and the same caveat: applied by hand via talosctl, outside Kustomize and Flux.

Cilium version the bootstrap cilium install lays down. Deliberately tracked as the SAME dep as the 05-cilium HelmRelease chart (datasource helm, name cilium) so Renovate bumps both in one PR instead of letting them drift -- a mismatch means first boot installs one Cilium and Flux immediately upgrades it to another. The capture group omits the leading v so it matches the chart version exactly; the v stays literal in the file because the CLI flag requires it.

Pinned CI tool versions in .github/workflows, comment-driven like the Ansible manager. These are plain `curl` downloads of release binaries, so no built-in manager sees them. Before this existed the pins drifted by hand and two of them were not pins at all -- Trivy came from an install.sh on the main branch and yq from /releases/latest -- which made CI unreproducible and, in Trivy's case, executed unversioned remote code.

packageRules.description: Keep CloudNativePG on the PostgreSQL 16 series. A major version change there is a database upgrade with its own migration path, not an image bump, and must never arrive as an automated PR.

The built-in kubernetes manager line-matches every `image:` field in any /cluster/.+\.yaml$ file regardless of `kind:`, so without this it independently proposes bumps to the talosctl image tags inside the SUC Plan files (talos-controlplane/worker/on-demand/kubernetes-upgrade.yaml). Those are Kustomize `replacements` placeholders now (config/kustomization.yaml), not pins -- a bump from this manager would edit a value that gets overwritten at build time anyway, in an ungrouped PR unrelated to the versions.env-driven update.

Block system-upgrade-controller chart 110.0.0 -- it is WITHDRAWN. It was published once, applied here as Helm release .v3, and pulled from https://rancher.github.io/charts afterwards. The index now carries 17 versions, newest 109.0.2. Flux cannot resolve it: the HelmChart sits Stalled on 'no chart with version matching 110.0.0 found', and a stalled chart cannot re-render, so every change to that HelmRelease applies cleanly to the object and silently never reaches the cluster (see #396). Renovate keeps offering it because it tracks the GitHub repo, where the tag still exists, rather than the chart index -- so the version it proposes is one that cannot be installed. Excluded as a semver range with a hole rather than a ceiling, so a genuine 110.0.1 is still offered if Rancher republishes -- pinning below 110 would silently freeze this chart at 109 forever.

Group the CLUSTER's Talos updates into one PR: versions.env's TALOS_VERSION and the machineconfig installer tag. Those two must move together -- talos-image-check fails a PR where they disagree -- so splitting them would produce a PR that fails its own check. The talosctl IMAGE in the SUC Plans needs no manager of its own: it is the same Kustomize-replacements field as TALOS_VERSION (see config/kustomization.yaml), so it cannot drift. The workstation talosctl BINARY in bootstrap/ is deliberately NOT in this group -- see the talos-cli rule at the end of this list.
Kubernetes control-plane version -- tracked and upgraded independently of Talos, never auto-merged (control-plane component upgrade).
Label major updates — CI workflow uses this to skip Trivy auto-merge
Label minor/patch updates — CI Trivy gate evaluates auto-merge eligibility
Disable digest updates for Talos images
Group Flux updates
Route all patch updates through Trivy gate (no Renovate-side automerge)

Split the admin workstation's talosctl CLI out of the cluster Talos group. bootstrap/ansible/group_vars/all.yml pins a BINARY downloaded onto a laptop (roles/homelab-tools fetches talosctl-{os}-{arch} from the release). That is a different artifact from the cluster's OS version, it touches no node, and it cannot break an upgrade. The rule grouping all siderolabs/talos updates has a rationale written about the ghcr.io/siderolabs/talosctl IMAGE in the SUC Plans -- which genuinely is driven by the same Kustomize replacement as TALOS_VERSION. The workstation binary was swept in only because it resolves to the same GitHub release. Talos supports client/server skew (a reboot on 2026-09-05 printed 'server version 1.13.0 is older than client version 1.13.6' as a normal warning), so these need not move together -- and bundling them puts a laptop tool bump in the same PR that reboots the cluster.

Never bump the postgres backup client across a major. These three images run pg_dump against keycloak-pg, filer-meta-pg and immich-postgresql, and each must match its server's major: pg_dump emits SQL for its OWN version, with no target-version flag and no down-conversion, so a dump taken by a newer client can fail to replay into an older server. On 2026-09-05 Renovate moved all three to 18 -- two majors ahead of two of the servers. Nothing caught it, because the DUMP direction kept working and the read-back checks kept passing; the failure would have appeared for the first time during an actual restore. Renovate cannot know these versions are coupled to a server it never sees, so the coupling is enforced here. Patch and minor updates within the pinned major still flow normally.

Never auto-merge the components that cannot be recovered from inside the cluster (ADR-009). A bad image in the network layer, the storage layer or remote access removes the means of fixing it: no CNI means no scheduling, no CSI means no volumes, and no Tailscale means no remote path in once the LAN one is gone. Size of the version step is irrelevant -- a patch can break a datapath as thoroughly as a major. manual-review is the label the Trivy auto-merge gate already refuses on, so this reuses that mechanism rather than adding one.

Kyverno ships five images from one release -- four controllers plus the admission init container -- and the chart that wires them. ADR-009 requires they move as one change: a deployment running mismatched Kyverno components is a worse failure than one that is a version behind.

Tailscale's operator and proxy images ship as one release, with the chart. Grouped so they cannot diverge. Also carries manual-review from the unrecoverable-component rule -- losing the operator removes the remote path into the cluster.
kubeopencode's controller and server are two roles of one binary, pinned twice from the same repository. Grouped so a bump cannot land on one and not the other.

Longhorn's ten images move as one group. The four longhorn-* images are one release, and the six CSI sidecars are republished by longhornio and version-matched to it -- upstream csi-attacher and Longhorn's build of it are not interchangeable. A CSI driver assembled from mismatched sidecars fails at volume attach, which here means every workload with a PVC. Also carries manual-review from the unrecoverable-component rule.

Stop the built-in kubernetes manager trying to resolve the Talos factory installer image. machine.install.image is a real YAML key, so that manager claims it and attempts a Docker lookup on factory.talos.dev/installer/<schematic-id> -- which has no tag list to enumerate, because the path segment is a content hash of the schematic rather than a repository name. The lookup fails with no-result and Renovate reports "Some dependencies could not be looked up" on every PR it opens. The version is already tracked, correctly, by the custom manager that reads the same line as siderolabs/talos from github-releases, so nothing is lost by silencing this one -- the line simply has two managers claiming it and only one that can resolve it. Scoped to the manager as well as the package so a future custom manager could still track this registry if needed.

Move the victoria-metrics chart and its pinned images together. ADR-009 requires a chart and the images it packages to move in one change. The chart's appVersion and the pinned tags describe the same release, so a proposal that carries one without the other opens a window where the pin is a downgrade of the chart's own intent. Grouping by package file keeps them in a single branch whenever both updates are available together.
Move the grafana chart and its pinned images together. See the victoria-metrics rule above for the reasoning; ADR-009 requires this for every chart.
